quote_or_note: Oracle's acquisition of Sun completed (infobox: "Completed January 27, 2010"). Primary press release 404 and AP copy at phys.org 403 on 2026-11-23; not retried.
"From now on, the OpenOffice.org community will be known as \"The Document Foundation\"". Oracle "has been invited to become a member ... and donate the brand".
In the announcement: Canonical ("the Ubuntu Project will be pleased to ship LibreOffice"), Google, Novell, Red Hat, FSF, OSI, GNOME Foundation, NeoOffice.
LibreOffice 3.3 (date from the post's address and title).
"the first major distribution to ship LibreOffice 3.3.1". LWN (https://lwn.net/Articles/432758/): "some of the folks behind LibreOffice are involved with openSUSE", so coded not independent.

Fedora 15 GA (date from https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Releases/HistoricalSchedules); the acceptance date was not found, so the release date is used. Reason: "a fork of OpenOffice(R) with the support of the OpenOffice.org(R) community"; "can continue without hampering from Oracle(R) should it decide to kill the project".
"On 1 June 2011, Oracle Corporation submitted the OpenOffice.org code base to The Apache Software Foundation". The name stayed with the original line.
Oracle's acquisition of Sun (MySQL's steward since 2008) announced ("Initiated April 20, 2009"). Widenius left Sun in February 2009, before it; the move is the one Fedora's later decision names.
First release, MariaDB 5.1.38 Beta ("Release date: 29 Oct 2009"); no earlier dated announcement of the fork was found.
MariaDB 5.1.38 Beta.

FESCo: "Fedora prefers MariaDB (+7,-0)"; accepted "including obsoletion as a transition mechanism". Reasons on https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Features/ReplaceMySQLwithMariaDB: Oracle "no longer publishing any useful information about security issues"; MariaDB "founded by some of the original MySQL developers, has a more open-source attitude". The devel-list proposal (2013-01-21) sits behind a bot check and was not read.
Wikimedia completed its move to MariaDB; "the move also visibly lends the Foundation's support to the MariaDB open-source project" (Signpost, reporting the Wikimedia blog).
Fedora 19 GA.
First dated report found of the dispute (it began in November 2010): "Oracle controls the Hudson project trademark".

"The final result of all eligible votes is as follows: 214 votes to rename, and 14 for the status quo." The infrastructure (lists, Twitter, GitHub organization) was to move "in the coming days", after the vote.
"it means Jenkins lives"
"Oracle abruptly changed course today and handed Hudson over to the open source Eclipse Foundation" (article of May 4, 2011; Wikipedia gives the proposal as May 3).
Eclipse wiki: "Since Hudson is not maintained anymore, Jenkins is the replacement for it." Dated by the archive capture.
First dated report read: io.js's committee lists Node.js core team members and alumni. No discrete act of the steward is coded as the move: the founders name Joyent's continuing control.
io.js v1.0.0.
"TC members decide to move io.js to Node Foundation and the organization name will be renamed nodejs" (weekly update of May 15; the vote date of May 13 is from search reporting).
Node.js 4.0.0, which "combines both the Node.js project and io.js project in a single codebase" (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/announcements/foundation-v4-announce).
"on August 10th, 2023 ... HashiCorp switched the license for Terraform from the MPL to the Business Source License"
"we're proud to announce that we have created a fork of Terraform" after an appeal to revert; the manifesto preceded it (LWN, https://lwn.net/Articles/942346/, August 23).
Linux Foundation launches OpenTofu.
OpenTofu 1.6.0.
"Redis will no longer be distributed under the three-clause Berkeley Software Distribution (BSD)"
"Community maintainers, contributors, and users will continue collaborative development ... under the new Valkey name"
Backers in the announcement: AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle, Ericsson, Snap.
The Linux Foundation forms the project.
Valkey 7.2.5 ("Release Date: 2024-04-15").
F41 change proposal posted.

FESCo: Closed: Accepted. Reason on https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Changes/Replace_Redis_With_Valkey: "Obsolete Redis for Valkey due to Redis's license change to RASLv2/SSPL" and "Redis's shift to the Server Side Public License (SSPL) that Fedora does not allow". Fedora 41's release date was behind a bot check (fedorapeople.org) and is not coded.
"Adding the OSI-approved AGPL as an additional licensing option for Redis, starting with Redis 8"
"October 25th: A blog post was written on the Gitea blog, informing about the creation of a company named Gitea Ltd."
"We started Forgejo in reaction to control of Gitea being taken away from the community by the newly-formed for-profit company Gitea Ltd"
Codeberg e.V. becomes custodian and "will use Forgejo as the basis for their own services, instead of Gitea".
Forgejo v1.18.0-1.
"On May 19, the staff resignations started being posted"; Lee, "owner of freenode since 2017", asserted control. No earlier dated act of the steward is coded.
Libera.Chat "introduced on that same fateful day", "staffed by former freenode volunteers".
SourceHut: "We entirely reject the illegitimate new leaders"; "We will be moving our channels to Libera Chat, effective today."
Update of 2021-05-25: "The new staff at Freenode have been re-opening channels which moved to Libera.chat". LWN: channels mentioning Libera were taken over.

Ubuntu "abruptly jumped ship to Libera Chat" after "what the Ubuntu Community Council described as a \"hostile takeover\" of its namespaces"; Wikimedia the same day; "the move had been on the cards" since the resignations.
"RethinkDB is shutting down" (the company).
"CNCF has purchased the source code to the RethinkDB database, relicensed the code under the Apache License ... and contributed it to The Linux Foundation."
The Linux Foundation as the new home.
"the first release since RethinkDB transitioned to community governance" (2.3.6).
Muse Group's acquisition reported (article of May 4; search reporting gives the announcement as May 3).

Users "arguing that the best course of action was to create a new fork" after the telemetry proposal and a new privacy policy. The fork's own first release was not dated (its release page listed nothing readable).
The new maintainer's first dated act: flatmap-stream "added as a direct dependency of the event-stream package by a new maintainer on September 9, 2018". The handover itself is not separately dated.
npm removed the malicious versions and took "ownership of the event-stream package to prevent further abuse".
